submission.natural_language_explanation: L11/N481+ is a retrospective specialist-register detector: inside a passage whose vocabulary comes from a learned scientific, mathematical, computing or biomedical domain it fires on the word-piece that carries the specialist term (Gaussian, Fourier, elliptic, synaptic, dendritic, mitochondrial, polymerase, vesicle, purpura, fluorescence, quantum, receptor, compiler, dereference, tensor) or on the word immediately beside it, and it strengthens as more such terms accumulate in the passage. Everyday and narrative prose, and general or institutional vocabulary (kettle, garden, government, market, hospital, information), leave it at zero, so the technicality of the passage - not token rarity, token length, or the token's position inside its word - is what decides.

rival_explanations: The pole is a construction detector rather than a vocabulary detector: it fires on the agentive preposition ' by' (or ' BY') after a formal past participle such as published, provided, produced or employed, so it fires on 'The report was published by the ministry' and stays at zero in a specialist passage that has no such construction.

The pole detects the legal and institutional register of licence and copyright boilerplate, so it fires on any GPL or copyright notice whatever its vocabulary and stays near zero on scientific, mathematical and biomedical prose.

Governor Bev Perdue has proclaimed Sept. 9 as Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder Awareness Day in North Carolina, and to help spread the word about the dangers of drinking while pregnant, the Connections Family Program partnered with Alcohol and Drug Services to present an educational workshop on Thursday.
A group of more than 20 participants who frequently work with women gathered at First United Methodist Church in Rockingham to hear a presentation by Amy Hendricks, project director for the North Carolina Fetal Alcohol Prevention Program. The program is a part of Mission Hospital’s Fullerton Genetics Center out of Asheville.
“My goal is to educate members of the community about the serious effects that alcohol can cause when a woman drinks during pregnancy,” Hendricks said. “These problems include physical, cognitive, behavioral and developmental disabilities which can affect an individual over a lifespan, requiring the services of many community agencies.”
During Thursday’s workshop, Hendricks discussed the effects of Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder, including its most well-known subgroup, Fetal Alcohol Syndrome. Also included under FASD are Alcohol-Related Birth Defects, Alcohol-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder and Partial Fetal Alcohol Syndrome.
“These workshops usually attract nurses, social workers, substance abuse counselors, and at least one or two caregivers,” said Substance Abuse Prevention Consultant Brenda David of Alcohol and Drug Services in Rockingham.
Hendricks provided national and statewide statistics involving FASD, noting that approximately 1 in 100 births in the United States are affected by the disorder, the equivalent of about 40,000 newborns.
The disorder can lead to birth defects, intellectual disabilities, learning disabilities, behavioral disorders and attention deficits, and is the only 100 percent preventable birth-defect, according to the North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services.
“Alcohol is such an accepted thing now,” Hendricks said to the group. “Our society is saturated with alcohol advertising and delivering the message that it’s all good.” The problem arrives, Hendricks said, when it reaches youth and pregnant woman.
Hendricks urged the importance of serving size when drinking alcohol, and how easy it is to misjudge its effectiveness on the body.
“We have to be mindful and help women understand servings,” said Hendricks. “As well as to increase awareness … it is harder for women to metabolize alcohol than men … If that woman is pregnant, that can increase fetus exposure to Fetal Alcohol Syndrome.”
Hendricks explained that alcohol is considered a Teratogen, a substance that can induce abnormalities of development with a developing embryo or fetus.
“Prenatal exposure to Teratogens like alcohol can cause premature birth, pre- and postnatal growth retardation, physical malformations, Sudden Infant Death Syndrome and cognitive and behavioral problems,” she said.

I can still remember the angst I went through as my daughter approached kindergarten, trying to decide whether to send her or hold her back another year, and in the decade since I’ve watched countless friends wrestle with the same question.
It is a dilemma that taints the joy of the preschool years and causes unnecessary anxiety for many families whose children are born in the first half of the calendar year.
Parents tend to assume that any difficulty a four-year old experiences in preschool is an indication they are not ready for school. The culture is to delay kindergarten and only parents who send their kids “on time” feel the need to defend their decision. All children must be in school by the time they turn six, however a child can start kindergarten in the year they turn five, if their birthday is before July 31. And this imposes a burden of choice on parents. Last year, most children born before this cut-off date were held back a year.
Yet University of New England research shows that any academic gains experienced by those starting school later disappear by the time those children reach Year 9. And in a starting-block blow for the equality that education is supposed to advance, it is wealthier families who can afford the choice of a delayed start.
It is clear the current system needs to be overhauled, to take the burden of decision-making away from parents and to ensure a more equitable schooling system.
Yes, there are social and educational differences in the early years but the current system exacerbates them by allowing a 19-month age gap in the same year group. Most four-year olds will, understandably, be outpaced and outsmarted by their six-year old “peers”.
Mantras like “every child is different” and “choice is essential” are being put ahead of common sense and a system that works. In community and school sports, strict 12-month age ranges apply to competition and “playing down” is an offence. Yet, in academic learning, parents are not only welcome to play their child down but are praised for doing so.
I propose a simple system to address these inequities: that all children start school the year after they turn five. This fits with research that four-and-a-half is too young to start school, now that the first year of school is no longer play-based, and follows trends towards later starting ages in Australia and overseas.
There should be leeway for children who need schooling brought forward or delayed. But this should be a tiny minority, with a clear assessment process involving parents, preschool educators and specialists.
Let’s make this a national system and ensure all children receive the best preparation for kindergarten through government-subsidised, play-based preschool programs.
Tightening the school age will eliminate unnecessary angst, freeing parents and children to embrace the joys of the preschool years and the milestone of starting school.
Vivienne Pearson is a freelance writer.

ATP participates in the oxidization of luciferin by the enzyme firefly luciferase, a reaction that produces light. The quantity of light produced is proportional to the quantity of luciferin oxidized. This reaction is very popular in reporter gene assays, where ATP and luciferin are in excess, and the quantity or light produced is limited by the expression of luciferase (the reporter). However, the same reaction can be used to quantify ATP if both luciferin and luciferase are in excess.
ATP measurements are used to monitor raw materials, manufacturing plant or food, drugs and healthcare equipment for bacterial contamination, often for, as well as for waste water analysis.
In the biotechnology and pharmaceutical industries, ATP measurements are used to evaluate cell proliferation, apoptosis and cytotoxicity. Cell viability assays, e.g. in tumour chemosensitivity assays and antibiotic susceptibility testing and determination of enzymes and metabolites in ATP-linked reactions can be performed. The bioluminescent assay of ATP has become very popular because of its high sensitivity and convenience.

Morelia, Michoacán.- El Observatorio Ciudadano de Michoacán (OCM), exhortó al Gobierno del Estado modificar la estrategia de seguridad, pues los delitos de secuestro, robo a casa habitación, robo a negocio y extorsión incrementaron en el segundo trimestre de 2018, lo que posiciona a la entidad entre los primeros lugares a nivel nacional.
Durante la presentación del informe trimestral, la organización civil observó que tan sólo en materia de secuestro, la entidad arrojó un incremento de 42.8 por ciento los casos, en casa habitación un 12.6 por ciento, en robo a negocio en un 4.4 por ciento y en extorsión un 100 por ciento, esto comparando el primer y segundo trimestre de la actual anualidad.
En tanto que el homicidio doloso, Michoacán tiene un reporte de 6.21 carpetas de investigación abiertas por cada 100 mil habitantes, mientras que la media nacional fue de 5.76, en total hubo 397 víctimas, lo que coloca al estado como el treceavo a nivel nacional en la incidencia de este delito.
(Foto: Especial)
Otra infracción que consideraron alarmante es el homicidio doloso donde la tasa de registro por cada 100 mil habitantes fue de 4.8, por lo que el estado ocupa el quinto lugar nacional en este tipo de incidentes que en su mayoría están ligados a incidentes de tránsito (144), arma de fuego (25) y el resto con otro tipo de circunstancias, destacando que en dos casos no especifican las condiciones en que fallecieron las víctimas.
Dentro de los homicidios, clasificaron aquellos eventos que estuvieron ligados con mujeres, en donde destacaron que el estado de Michoacán cuenta con tres carpetas de investigación sobre feminicidios durante el segundo trimestre del presente año. Con esta cifra la entidad se coloca en el número 24 del ranking nacional.
Las cifras anteriores provienen del informe del Secretariado Ejecutivo del Sistema Nacional de la Seguridad Pública, en el segundo trimestre del 2018, Michoacán registra una constante en la incidencia delictiva desde inicios del presente año, lo que deja entrever la estrategia fallida que aplican las autoridades para el combate de los delitos del fuero federal y común, así lo comentó Rodrigo Antúnez Álvarez, integrante del observatorio.
“Estamos estancados desde el inicio de año, no hemos tenido una mejora clara en los índices (de incidencia delictiva)”, y reiteró que se mantiene el “alza en robo a casa habitación, robo a negocio y extorsión” observó Antúnez Álvarez al retomar las cifras en estos temas.
En la exposición indicó que en materia de extorsión, hubo una carpeta de investigación, ocupando el lugar 30 a nivel nacional con 0.02 carpetas por cada 100 mil habitantes; lo cual pudiera considerarse positivo a no ser que el robo con violencia se recrudeció durante el trimestre semestre del año ya que existe un registraron mil 749 carpetas de investigación, posicionando a la entidad en el lugar 12 a nivel nacional con 37.31 carpetas por cada 100 mil habitantes.

readings.explanation: L11/N481+ is a retrospective specialist-register detector: inside a passage whose vocabulary comes from a learned scientific, mathematical, computing or biomedical domain it fires on the word-piece that carries the specialist term (Gaussian, Fourier, elliptic, synaptic, dendritic, mitochondrial, polymerase, vesicle, purpura, fluorescence, quantum, receptor, compiler, dereference, tensor) or on the word immediately beside it, and it strengthens as more such terms accumulate in the passage. Everyday and narrative prose, and general or institutional vocabulary (kettle, garden, government, market, hospital, information), leave it at zero, so the technicality of the passage - not token rarity, token length, or the token's position inside its word - is what decides.

The pole is a construction detector rather than a vocabulary detector: it fires on the agentive preposition ' by' (or ' BY') after a formal past participle such as published, provided, produced or employed, so it fires on 'The report was published by the ministry' and stays at zero in a specialist passage that has no such construction.

The pole detects the legal and institutional register of licence and copyright boilerplate, so it fires on any GPL or copyright notice whatever its vocabulary and stays near zero on scientific, mathematical and biomedical prose.
